clue.text: Avoiding action first under 17,19 by rail, we hear

definitions.meaning: to run a mile from something is the idiom for steering well clear of it

definitions.text: first under 17,19 by rail, we hear
definitions.meaning: Roger Bannister was first to cover the distance in under four minutes, and his surname sounds like banister, a stair rail

explanation.surface: A commuter dodges trouble, apparently first under some deadline on the train.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is the theme: Roger Bannister ran the first four-minute mile in 1954, and 'by rail, we hear' puns on his name sounding like banister.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom of fleeing far from something stands for taking evasive steps to avoid it.

clue.text: Stand where there are no traffic lights

definitions.meaning: to stand something is to endure or put up with it

definitions.text: where there are no traffic lights
definitions.meaning: the green go signal is the bottom lamp of a set, so there are no lights beneath it

explanation.surface: A pedestrian waits at a crossing with no signals.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the word into UNDER + GO: green, the go light, is the lowest lamp, with nothing below it.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand hardship is to endure it, the same sense as going through an experience.

clue.text: Notice of strike in 17,19

parts.note: the British Cold War public alert was to give four minutes of notice before a missile attack

explanation.surface: A union posts notice of a walkout with minutes to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests industrial action, but it is a military attack: Britain's Cold War siren system promised a four-minute warning of incoming missiles.
explanation.definitionFit: An alert of an atomic attack is exactly a notice that a strike is coming.

clue.text: Retreat from everyone's thoughts

indicators.note: from means the letters are drawn out of the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone withdraws from what everybody is thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosy refuge or hideaway is a retreat, like a bird's home.

clue.text: Compromises in meat and greens dispute

indicators.note: a dispute stirs things up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A family settles a quarrel over meat versus vegetables at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Compromises are deals or settlements reached between parties, i.e. accords.

clue.text: King signals early return to country

indicators.note: return asks for these pieces to be read from right to left

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's monarch

indicators.note: this word picks out the opening letter, or opening letters, of the words it governs

explanation.surface: A monarch's early signals mark his homecoming to his realm.
explanation.definitionFit: A Middle Eastern nation, so an example of a country.

clue.text: Measure pub spirit with restraint

parts.note: an em is a printer's measure of width
a bar is a pub or drinking place
go means spirit, energy or verve

explanation.surface: Someone measures out pub spirits sparingly.
explanation.definitionFit: A ban on trade is a restraint imposed by a government.

clue.text: Madonna's son that Harry's hit (first one over 17,19)

definitions.text: Madonna's son that Harry's hit (first one over 17,19)

parts.words: Madonna's son that Harry's hit (first one over 17,19)
parts.note: the Virgin Mary's infant is the title of Harry Belafonte's 1956 Christmas hit, the first single longer than four minutes

explanation.surface: Gossip about a pop star's son and a royal's hit record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Madonna' and 'Harry' suggest the singer and the prince, but they are the Virgin Mary and Harry Belafonte, whose carol was the first UK chart-topper over four minutes long.
explanation.definitionFit: The Virgin's infant son is named literally, and the phrase is also a famous carol title.

clue.text: Urgently sling out perfect breakfast made in 17,19

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order, rearranged

explanation.surface: A rushed cook flings out a breakfast timed to four minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: A four-minute boiled egg leaves the yolk soft.
explanation.definitionFit: Boiling an egg for four minutes gives a soft yolk, the classic ideal breakfast.

clue.text: Sailor pipes spirits away

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
ducts are pipes or channels

explanation.surface: A sailor's piping summons ghosts away.
explanation.definitionFit: To spirit someone away is to carry them off secretly, i.e. kidnap.

clue.text: Chewed on red cheese dish

parts.note: rare meat is red inside, barely cooked
bit is the past tense of bite, so chewed on

explanation.surface: Someone munches a red cheese snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is melted cheese on toast, a savoury cheese dish.

clue.text: Lengthy delivery which may result in one walking out

definitions.text: Lengthy delivery which may result in one walking out

parts.words: Lengthy delivery which may result in one walking out
parts.note: in cricket, a ball pitched full length at the batsman's feet that often bowls him, sending him off

explanation.surface: A long speech that might prompt someone in the audience to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' is a cricket ball, not a speech; a full-length ball aimed at the toes often gets the batter out, and an out batter walks off.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket ball pitched right at the feet is a full-length delivery that can dismiss a batsman.

clue.text: Adjournment makes both sides deafer

indicators.note: makes signals the letters being worked into something new

parts.note: R and L, right and left, are both sides

explanation.surface: Postponing a hearing apparently leaves everyone harder of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting off a matter to a later date is a postponement or adjournment.

clue.text: Left car in direction detailed on the canvas

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other
detailed means the tail, the last letter, is cut off

parts.note: south is a compass direction
to leave a car somewhere is to park it

explanation.surface: Someone leaves their car facing a given way, sketched on an artist's canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canvas' looks artistic but it is the boxing ring floor, where a knocked-out fighter lies.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer knocked out cold lies flat on the ring floor, the canvas.

clue.text: Ghost maybe of many life sentences

definitions.text: Ghost maybe of many life sentences

parts.words: Ghost maybe of many life sentences
parts.note: a ghostwriter of life stories pens many sentences about other people's lives

explanation.surface: A phantom haunts a prison full of lifers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Life sentences' suggests prison, but it means sentences written about a life, often by a ghostwriter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes accounts of people's lives, possibly as a hired ghost.

clue.text: Wind flop up

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to sag is to droop or flop

explanation.surface: A wind dies and the sails flop.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatulence is called wind, or gas.

clue.text: Report somewhat variform in its time

indicators.note: a report is a spoken account, so we want what these letters sound like
somewhat means only part of the run of words is taken

explanation.surface: A report on something taking various forms over the years.
explanation.definitionFit: A short stretch of minutes is a span of time.

clue.text: Overweight from regular feasts

indicators.note: regular means taking every other letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Frequent banquets leave someone overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump or obese, carrying excess weight.

clue.text: Roots around in dismay

indicators.note: around means the letters run back to front
in means the letters lie inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone digs about in dismay.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible tubers, sweet potatoes, are root vegetables.

clue.text: See 17 across
Can critter overhaul record breaking winger?

indicators.note: an overhaul takes something apart and rebuilds it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Could an animal reshape the record-setting rugby wing?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a sports player, but it is a bird; this seabird makes the longest migration of any animal.
explanation.definitionFit: This polar seabird holds the record for the longest annual migration.

clue.text: Energetically heads to celebration of City follower of note

indicators.note: follower of means the city's piece comes straight after the note's piece
heads to means the first letters of the following words

parts.note: NB, nota bene, is a written note meaning take note
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian city, often just Rio

explanation.surface: Fans cheer their City team with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City follower' looks like a football fan, but 'follower of note' puts RIO after NB, the abbreviation for nota bene.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning with vigour and spirit.

clue.text: Object to factory a bit

parts.note: an end is an object or aim
a mill is a factory

explanation.surface: Someone protests against a factory a little.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting tool fitted to a milling machine, a type of drill bit.

clue.text: Initially, you only might take one villa holiday

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A traveller ponders taking a single villa for a getaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish festival day on which work is forbidden, i.e. a holiday.

clue.text: Depend on result of wasted time

parts.note: to hang on is to depend, so hang alone carries that sense
over means on, as in resting on top

explanation.surface: Relying on the outcome of time frittered away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' means drunk: a sore head the morning after.
explanation.definitionFit: The morning-after misery that follows a drunken night out.

clue.text: Eventually or from time to time

definitions.meaning: at some point in the future
a stretch running from one point of the clock round to the same point next morning

explanation.surface: Something happens at last, or now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Some day in the future means eventually; a span of twenty-four hours runs from a time to that time.

clue.text: Precious material cut

indicators.note: cut means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: tweed is a woven woollen material

explanation.surface: Valuable fabric gets trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Affectedly dainty or quaint, overly cute.

clue.text: Forget it's how linesmen treat illegal catch

definitions.meaning: to drop the matter and stop dwelling on it
anglers with lines release an undersized or protected fish

explanation.surface: Football officials told to ignore an illegal catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Linesmen' suggests sports officials, but here they are anglers, who must release a fish they may not keep.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means drop the matter, and literally describes releasing a fish.

clue.text: See 3
8's pursuit of lover wasted openheart surgery (Madonna had 17,19)

indicators.note: surgery cuts up and rearranges, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: the opening of heart is its first letter

explanation.surface: A jilted lover's wasted heart operation, with a pop star's song added.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is Mary's boy child, Jesus, whose mission was to redeem humanity; Madonna's song was '4 Minutes (To Save the World)'.
explanation.definitionFit: The mission of the Christ child was to redeem humanity.
